title: Analysis of RNA-containing compartments by hybridization and proximity labeling in cultured human cells
author: Yap, Chung, et al.

Data are normalized to the GAPDH ”housekeeping“ mRNA and the abundance of (C) 45S or (D) NEAT1 in total RNA inputs. The analyses were done in triplicate and presented as means ± SD. steps.title: Transform E. coli with HyPro plasmid
steps.instruction: Transform chemically competent SoluBL21 E. coli (AMSBIO) with the pML433 plasmid (Addgene #177190) and plate on LB agar containing 25 µg/mL kanamycin; incubate at 37 °C overnight (~16 h).

steps.title: Grow single colony overnight
steps.instruction: Pick a single colony and inoculate 4 mL LB broth with 25 µg/mL kanamycin; grow at 37 °C with shaking at 250 rpm overnight (~16 h).

steps.title: Scale up culture to OD600 0.6
steps.instruction: Dilute the overnight culture into 600 mL fresh LB broth with 25 µg/mL kanamycin in a 2‑L conical flask; shake at 37 °C until OD600 reaches 0.6 (≈3 h).

steps.title: Induce HyPro expression with IPTG
steps.instruction: Chill the culture on ice for 10 min, add IPTG to a final concentration of 0.5 mM (Promega), and continue shaking at 25 °C for 24 h to express HyPro protein.

steps.title: Harvest bacterial cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the culture at 10,000×g for 10 min at 4 °C; decant most supernatant and tap the tube on a paper towel to remove residual liquid. (Pause: pellets can be stored at –80 °C up to 1 month.)

steps.title: Lyse cells with BugBuster and enzymes
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 45 mL BugBuster protein extraction reagent (≈15 mL per 1 g wet pellet) supplemented with 1500 U/mL rLysozyme and 25 U/mL benzonase (Millipore); incubate 20–24 °C for 30 min with rotation. Set aside a few µL for SDS‑PAGE and store lysate at –80 °C until needed.

steps.title: Clarify lysate by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate at 16,000×g for 20 min at 4 °C; keep a few µL of supernatant for SDS‑PAGE and store the remainder at –80 °C.

steps.title: Filter lysate through 0.45 µm filter
steps.instruction: Pass the clarified supernatant through a 0.45‑µm low‑protein‑binding syringe filter.

steps.title: Bind HyPro to HisTrap columns
steps.instruction: Load the filtered supernatant onto two sequentially connected 1‑mL HisTrap FF Crude columns (GE Healthcare) equilibrated with buffer A (20 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0, 100 mM NaCl, 25 mM imidazole, 14 mM β‑mercaptoethanol) at 1 mL/min.

steps.title: Wash HisTrap columns
steps.instruction: Wash the columns with 20 mL of buffer A at 1 mL/min.

steps.title: Elute HyPro protein from HisTrap
steps.instruction: Elute His‑tagged HyPro with a 1:1 mixture of buffer A and buffer B (20 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0, 100 mM NaCl, 500 mM imidazole, 14 mM β‑ME) at 0.5 mL/min.

steps.title: Perform size‑exclusion chromatography
steps.instruction: Load the 6 mL HisTrap eluate onto a HiLoad 26/60 Superdex 75 column (GE Healthcare) equilibrated with buffer C (20 mM Tris pH 8.0, 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT) at 1 mL/min; elute with buffer C at 2 mL/min, collecting 1‑mL fractions. (Pause: store fractions at 4 °C for 24–48 h.)

steps.title: Analyze fractions by SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Run each collected fraction on SDS‑PAGE and stain with Coomassie R‑250.

steps.title: Quantify and pool HyPro fractions
steps.instruction: Determine protein concentration using a Pierce BCA Kit (Thermo Fisher) as instructed; pool the peak fractions that contain high HyPro and minimal contaminants.

steps.title: Aliquot and store purified HyPro
steps.instruction: Aliquot the pooled HyPro protein, snap‑freeze in liquid nitrogen, and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Spin decrosslinked lysate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the decrosslinked lysate at 15,000×g for 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant and optional input
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to a new tube; optionally set aside 10 % of the lysate as an input fraction. Lysates can be stored at –80 °C.

steps.title: Wash streptavidin beads
steps.instruction: Wash 60 µL of MyOne streptavidin C1 magnetic beads twice with Regular‑SDS RIPA buffer.

steps.title: Bind biotinylated proteins to beads
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed beads in 3 mL Regular‑SDS RIPA buffer, add ~600 µL lysate (6‑fold dilution), and incubate at 20–24 °C for 2 h with rotation (or overnight ~16 h at 4 °C).

steps.title: Collect beads after binding
steps.instruction: Pellet the beads using a DynaMag™‑2 magnet and discard the supernatant (optionally save supernatant for troubleshooting).

steps.title: Stringent wash of protein‑bead complex
steps.instruction: Wash the beads sequentially with:

substeps.instruction: 2 M urea in 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0 – once

steps.title: Elute proteins with biotin‑containing buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend beads in 15 µL Regular‑SDS RIPA buffer supplemented with 1× cOmplete EDTA‑free protease inhibitor, 1 mM PMSF, 50 mM DTT and 5 mM biotin; incubate 20 min at 37 °C with gentle agitation.

steps.title: Add LDS sample buffer and denature
steps.instruction: Add 15 µL 4× LDS sample buffer containing 50 mM DTT to the beads and heat at 70 °C for 10 min.

steps.title: Collect supernatant for immunoblot
steps.instruction: Vortex, chill on ice, briefly spin down, then pellet beads with the magnet and transfer the supernatant to a new tube for SDS‑PAGE.

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE and transfer to membrane
steps.instruction: Separate proteins by SDS‑PAGE, transfer to a nitrocellulose membrane (e.g., Bio‑Rad Trans‑Blot Turbo), and block with 3 % BSA in 1× TBS + 0.1 % Tween‑20 for 30–60 min at 20–24 °C or overnight (~16 h) at 4 °C.

steps.title: Probe membrane with streptavidin‑HRP
steps.instruction: Incubate the blocked membrane with streptavidin‑HRP (1:20,000 in 1× TBS + 0.1 % Tween‑20) for 60 min at 20–24 °C or overnight (~16 h) at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash membrane and detect signal
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane four times with 1× TBS + 0.1 % Tween‑20, 5 min each at 20–24 °C, then visualize bands using enhanced chemiluminescence.

steps.title: Wash beads for mass‑spec prep
steps.instruction: Pellet the beads and wash three times with 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate.

steps.title: Digest proteins overnight with Trypsin/Lys‑C
steps.instruction: Resuspend beads in 45 µL 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate containing 1.5 µg Trypsin/Lys‑C (7.5 µL of 0.2 µg/µL stock diluted with 37.5 µL ammonium bicarbonate); incubate ~16 h at 37 °C with rotation.

steps.title: Perform second trypsin digestion
steps.instruction: Add an additional 0.75 µg Trypsin/Lys‑C (3.75 µL of 0.2 µg/µL stock diluted with 11.25 µL ammonium bicarbonate) and incubate 2 h at 37 °C with rotation.

steps.title: Collect peptide supernatant
steps.instruction: Pellet the beads and transfer the supernatant to a fresh tube.

steps.title: Wash beads and combine washes
steps.instruction: Wash beads twice with 45 µL mass‑spec grade water (total 90 µL) and combine these washes with the previously collected supernatant.

steps.title: Clarify peptide solution
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the combined solution at 14,000–16,000×g for 10 min; transfer the clear supernatant to a new tube.

steps.title: Submit peptides for mass spectrometry
steps.instruction: Send the clarified peptide solution for label‑free mass‑spectrometry analysis. (Critical: wear gloves to avoid keratin contamination.)

steps.title: Digest RNA with proteinase K
steps.instruction: Incubate the decrosslinked lysate (from step 30) with 20 µL of 20 mg/mL proteinase K at 37 °C for 20 min, then at 50 °C for 60 min.

steps.title: Add Trizol LS for RNA extraction
steps.instruction: Add three volumes of Trizol LS reagent to the digested lysate and mix thoroughly. (Pause: Trizol‑lysed samples can be stored at –80 °C up to 1 month.)

steps.title: Purify RNA with PureLink kit
steps.instruction: Purify RNA using the PureLink RNA Mini Kit (Thermo Fisher) following the manufacturer’s protocol, including on‑column DNase digestion.

steps.title: Elute RNA and set aside input
steps.instruction: Elute RNA with 100 µL nuclease‑free water; retain 10 µL of the eluate as an input fraction.

steps.title: Prepare streptavidin beads for RNA capture
steps.instruction: Use 20 µL MyOne streptavidin C1 beads per 50 µg total RNA. Wash beads sequentially:

substeps.instruction: 0.1 M NaOH + 0.05 M NaCl + 0.1 % Tween‑20 – once
0.1 M NaCl + 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5 + 1 mM EDTA + 0.2 % Tween‑20 – once

steps.title: Resuspend beads in binding buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed beads in 150 µL of 0.1 M NaCl, 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5, 1 mM EDTA, 0.2 % Tween‑20, and 0.2 units/µL RNase inhibitor.

steps.title: Combine beads with total RNA
steps.instruction: Mix the bead suspension with purified total RNA (90 µL from step 38 diluted with nuclease‑free water to 150 µL) to obtain ~300 µL of RNA‑bead slurry.

steps.title: Incubate RNA‑bead mixture
steps.instruction: Rotate the slurry at 4 °C for 2 h.

steps.title: Collect beads after capture
steps.instruction: Capture the beads with a DynaMag™‑2 magnet and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Wash beads post‑capture
steps.instruction: Wash the beads three times with B&W buffer.

steps.title: Digest RNA‑bead complexes with proteinase K
steps.instruction: Resuspend beads in 63 µL nuclease‑free water, 33 µL 3× protease digestion buffer, and 4 µL proteinase K (20 mg/mL).

steps.title: Incubate digestion at 50 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture at 50 °C for 45 min with agitation.

steps.title: Extract RNA with Trizol LS
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL Trizol LS (3 volumes), mix, and incubate 5 min.

steps.title: Phase separation with chloroform
steps.instruction: Add 80 µL chloroform per 400 µL Trizol mixture, vortex vigorously, and incubate at 20–24 °C for 2–3 min.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 15 min at 12,000×g at 4 °C; retain the aqueous phase.

steps.title: Clean up RNA with RNA‑Clean kit
steps.instruction: Purify RNA from the aqueous phase using an RNA Clean and Concentrator kit (Zymo Research) according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Elute purified RNA
steps.instruction: Elute the RNA in 15 µL nuclease‑free water.

steps.title: Validate enrichment by RT‑qPCR
steps.instruction: Use 1 µL of the eluate for RT‑qPCR to confirm enrichment of the target RNA. (Pause: store remaining RNA at –80 °C until library preparation.)

steps.title: (Optional) Quantify RNA with Qubit
steps.instruction: Measure RNA concentration using a Qubit RNA HS Assay kit, optionally adding an RNA spike‑in as described by Li et al. (2015).

steps.title: (Optional) Assess biotinylation via dot blot
steps.instruction: Perform an RNA dot blot (Abcam protocol) and detect biotinylated RNA with streptavidin‑HRP and ECL reagents.

steps.title: (Optional) Deplete rRNA and prepare sequencing libraries
steps.instruction: Deplete rRNA using a NEBNext rRNA Depletion Kit, then construct stranded libraries with the NEBNext Ultra II Directional RNA Library Prep Kit (Illumina) and barcoded primers; for 45S‑ and NEAT1‑labeled samples, use 18 PCR cycles during enrichment.

description: Eukaryotic cells assemble numerous macromolecular complexes and membraneless bodies containing RNA components (Alberti and Hyman, 2021; Bhat et al., 2021; Chujo and Hirose, 2017; Roden and Gladfelter, 2021; Wilkinson et al., 2020; Yusupova and Yusupov, 2014). Given the importance of RNA-protein interactions in health and disease and the pervasive transcription of mammalian genomes (Gebauer et al., 2021; Gil and Ulitsky, 2020; Quinn and Chang, 2016; Statello et al., 2021; Uszczynska-Ratajczak et al., 2018), understanding how RNA compartments form and function is an exciting research direction. We developed a hybridization-proximity (HyPro) labeling technology facilitating discovery of protein and RNA enriched within or near RNA-containing cellular compartments. This approach requires a custom-designed recombinant HyPro enzyme and digoxigenin-labeled probes, prepared and quality-controlled as described in this section. The protocol describes HyPro labeling of the 45S and NEAT1 RNAs in fixed and permeabilized HeLa cells followed by fluorescence imaging of proximity-labeled foci (HyPro-FISH) or purification of biotinylated proteins and RNAs for mass-spectrometry and RNA-seq (HyPro-MS and HyPro-seq). We have also used this protocol to analyze the 45S RNA in human iPS cells, NEAT1 in ARPE-19 cells and PNCTR in HeLa cells.
